cooktopTypes.name: Standard Residential Gas Cooktop (4 Burners)
cooktopTypes.description: Standard 30-inch 4-burner gas range consuming utility methane. Generates continuous NO2, carbon monoxide, and ultrafine combustion particles whenever active.

cooktopTypes.name: Pro-Style High-Output Gas Range (6 Burners + Griddle)
cooktopTypes.description: High-output commercial-style domestic range (36–48 inches). Produces severe thermal up-thrust and massive nitrogen dioxide surges capable of exceeding outdoor EPA air quality limits within 10 minutes without high-CFM extraction.

cooktopTypes.name: Smooth Ceramic Glass Radiant Electric Cooktop
cooktopTypes.description: Electric radiant heating elements underneath smooth ceramic glass. Produces zero combustion byproducts (0 NO2, 0 CO, 0 Benzene); air quality load consists entirely of culinary cooking aerosol emissions.

cooktopTypes.name: Modern Electromagnetic Induction Cooktop
cooktopTypes.description: Direct ferromagnetic pan heating via magnetic induction. 85–90% thermal efficiency means virtually no ambient convective waste heat spills around the cookware, keeping the thermal plume tight and low-velocity.

cookingProcesses.name: High-Heat Wok Searing & Sautéing (Steak / Stir-Fry)
cookingProcesses.description: High-temperature oil degradation above flash point generates dense aerosolized lipid droplets, acrolein fumes, and massive PM2.5 spikes (often >800 µg/m³).

cookingProcesses.name: Deep Frying (Chicken / French Fries)
cookingProcesses.description: Continuous bubble bursting aerosolizes microscopic oil mist droplets into the breathing zone, accompanied by volatile aldehydes and free fatty acids.

cookingProcesses.name: Shallow Pan Frying & Sautéing (Fish / Veggies)
cookingProcesses.description: Moderate heat sautéing. Generates moderate levels of fine particulates and cooking aromas that dissipate with standard capture rates.

cookingProcesses.name: Boiling, Steaming & Pasta Simmering
cookingProcesses.description: Water-phase cooking generates zero lipid particulates. Load consists of steam and latent humidity. However, with gas burners, combustion NO2 and CO remain fully present.

cookingProcesses.name: Oven High-Heat Roasting & Broiling
cookingProcesses.description: Oven vents exhaust fat aerosol plumes from the rear stovetop backsplash or beneath the control console, frequently bypassing shallow hoods entirely.

hoodTypes.name: Ducted Wall-Mount Chimney / Pyramid Canopy
hoodTypes.description: Gold standard residential design. Deep 20–24 inch projection over the cooktop and a 3-inch recessed sump contain thermal bursts until the high-CFM blower evacuates them outdoors.

hoodTypes.name: Ducted Under-Cabinet Range Hood (Pro-Style)
hoodTypes.description: Mounted beneath upper cabinetry. Offers good rear burner capture, but shallow forward overhang allows rapid plume escape if cooking at high boil or heavy sear on front burners.

hoodTypes.name: Over-The-Range (OTR) Microwave Hood (Ducted to Outside)
hoodTypes.description: Combination microwave oven with bottom intake fan. Lacks capture sump entirely; shallow 15-inch depth leaves front 12 inches of cooktop exposed. Front burner capture is notoriously poor (<45%).

hoodTypes.name: Ductless Recirculating Hood (Charcoal / Carbon Filter)
hoodTypes.description: Draws air through aluminum grease mesh and an activated charcoal pad, then exhausts it right back into the kitchen ceiling. Zero NO2, CO, or moisture removal; carbon filter rapidly saturates within 2-3 months.

hoodTypes.name: Ducted Island Chimney Hood (Suspended Ceiling)
hoodTypes.description: Suspended over open kitchen islands. Highly vulnerable to ambient cross-drafts (walking traffic, HVAC registers) because it lacks a rear wall to guide the thermal updraft. Requires 30–50% higher CFM to match wall hoods.

hoodTypes.name: Pop-Up Retractable Downdraft Vent
hoodTypes.description: Retracts behind rear burners. Fights fundamental buoyancy physics by attempting to pull rising hot air downward. Captures rear pans acceptably, but almost completely fails (>80% leakage) on tall stockpots or front burners.

filterTypes.name: Commercial Stainless Steel Baffle Filters
filterTypes.description: Interlocking curves force grease-laden air to change direction abruptly, flinging heavier aerosolized droplets into collection troughs. Lowest static pressure drop and optimal fire containment.

filterTypes.name: Multi-Layer Aluminum Mesh Filters
filterTypes.description: Staggered layers of perforated aluminum mesh catch grease droplets. Airflow drops significantly when saturated with sticky cooking oils; requires monthly cleaning to prevent CFM collapse.

filterTypes.name: Activated Carbon / Charcoal Recirculating Pad
filterTypes.description: Microporous activated charcoal adsorbs organic odors and volatile hydrocarbons. However, it imposes severe static pressure resistance, reducing blower CFM by 30–45%, and DOES NOT capture combustion NO2 or CO.

ductProfiles.name: 6-inch Diameter Smooth Galvanized Rigid Steel
ductProfiles.description: Standard minimum residential duct. Smooth galvanized wall minimizes turbulence. Rated up to 400 CFM without excessive static backpressure.

ductProfiles.name: 8-inch Diameter Smooth Galvanized Rigid Steel
ductProfiles.description: High-performance ductwork. 77% greater cross-sectional area than 6-inch pipe allows 600–900 CFM blowers to operate whisper-quiet with minimal backpressure loss.

ductProfiles.name: 10-inch Diameter Smooth Rigid Metal Duct
ductProfiles.description: Commercial-grade pro installation for 1000+ CFM blowers servicing high-output 6-burner gas ranges.

ductProfiles.name: 6-inch Flexible Corrugated Aluminum Accordion Duct
ductProfiles.description: Common DIY shortcut. Internal helical ridges create immense aerodynamic boundary turbulence and trap flammable grease pools, slashing effective blower CFM by up to 50%.

clinicalHazards: Causes bronchial hyper-responsiveness and airway inflammation within 15–30 minutes.
Meta-analysis (Gruenwald et al. 2023): Attributable to 12.7% of US childhood asthma cases.
Unvented gas stoves regularly create kitchen concentrations of 150–500 ppb NO2, exceeding EPA outdoor emergency limits.
Microscopic aerosolized oil droplets and soot penetrate deep into pulmonary alveoli and cross into capillary bloodstream.
High-heat wok searing in unventilated rooms produces PM2.5 spikes of 600–1400 µg/m³, equivalent to extreme hazardous wildfire smoke.
Associated with acute cardiovascular strain, platelet activation, and pediatric respiratory infections.
Kashtan et al. (Stanford 2023) demonstrated that gas burners emit unburned benzene from incomplete methane ignition.
Benzene concentrations in bedrooms can exceed chronic health benchmarks for hours after cooking without exterior exhaust venting.
Directly linked to leukemia, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and bone marrow cellular DNA damage.
